messages:
kevin: FYI AcmeCorp on Private is getting 502s when calling our embeddings endpoint. They say their corp LB does TLS terminate + re-encrypt. Report started right after they upgraded the LB crypto module.

sara: can you paste the client/server TLS logs they gave? any TLS alerts in our sidecar or the ingress logs?

kevin: customer sent this openssl probe from their LB to our upstream (redacted hostnames):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect upstream.internal:443 -servername embeddings.private.acme -alpn h2 -cipher ECDHE-ECDSA
CONNECTED(00000005)
depth=0 C = US, O = Acme, CN = upstream.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 360 bytes
140735219841984:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1526:SSL alert number 40
---

TLS debug: "no shared signature algorithm" and "handshake failure (40)"
```

kevin: their LB debug indicates the LB refuses to accept the upstream cert chain if it is ECDSA (they've got ECDSA only on our private endpoint). LB logs: "re-encrypt failed: unsupported sigalg: ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256". customer says their LB crypto module only supports RSA sigalg after the upgrade.

maria: that would explain 502 on re-encrypt. If LB terminates TLS and then attempts to create a new TLS session to our upstream but only offers RSA sigalgs, and our upstream cert is ECDSA-only, there is no compatible sigalg -> handshake fails.

infra-oncall: quick checks: 1) confirm our private endpoint cert type (ECDSA vs RSA) 2) check which sigalgs and curves we advertise. Can you run `openssl s_client -connect <private-host>:443 -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-ECDSA' -sigalgs` from a test host? Also check our cert chain: `openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout | grep -i public`.

kevin: ran a local probe from a jumpbox (our side):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private-ingest.redwood.internal:443 -servername embeddings.private.redwood -alpn h2
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=embeddings.private.redwood
   i:/CN=redwood-ecdsa-issuing
subjectPublicKeyInfo:
  Public Key Algorithm: id-ecPublicKey
  Public-Key: (256 bit)
  pub:
    04:...
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.2
    Cipher    : ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
```

kevin: so we serve an ECDSA cert and prefer ECDHE-ECDSA ciphers.

sara: two remediation paths: 1) customer re-enable ECDSA sigalgs/curves on LB (preferred), 2) we serve an RSA alternative cert for their private deployment (requires provisioning + devops PR). Which does customer want?

kevin: customer asked if we can flip to RSA cert on our side as a stop-gap. They don't want to change LB config without their security team's approval.

maria: we can provision an RSA cert for Private but need ticket to provisioning + rotation window. It will be treated like a key rotation (audit implications). I'll open a change request and estimate ~2 business days.

infra-oncall: in parallel, ask customer to capture the TCP dump of the upstream handshake and include the ClientHello from LB -> we want to confirm advertised sigalgs and curves. If they can run `openssl s_client -connect upstream.internal:443 -state -debug` it prints the handshake debug.

support-bot: Reminder: attach customer private deployment id and region so infra team can lookup cert in KC. (automation note).

kevin: I'll schedule a quick call with Acme infra engineer and cc infra-oncall. I'll attach their TCP/openssl captures when we have them.  :thumbsup:

maria: assigning change request CR-5678 to provisioning to add optional RSA cert for acme-private. Will update after approvals.

kevin: thanks — will follow up in this thread with the captures and the customer's decision.
